example.ja: レベル高すぎてついていけない。
example.english: The level's too high, I can't keep up.

examplePolite.romaji: Reberu ga takasugite, tsuite ikemasen.
examplePolite.ja: レベルが高すぎて、ついていけません。
examplePolite.english: The level is too high for me to keep up.

notes: Reberu ga takai = high standard, really good.

example.ja: いろんな種類があるね。

examplePolite.romaji: Iroiro na shurui ga arimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: いろいろな種類がありますね。

notes: Counts kinds directly: sanshurui = three kinds.

english: set (of things); meal set; setting up

example.romaji: Setto de kau to yasui yo.
example.ja: セットで買うと安いよ。
example.english: It's cheaper if you buy them as a set.

examplePolite.romaji: Setto de kau to yasui desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: セットで買うと安いですよ。
examplePolite.english: It's cheaper if you buy the set.

notes: Setto suru = set (an alarm) or set up; also a hair set at the salon.

use: Often means someone's handwriting: ji ga kirei = neat handwriting.

example.ja: 字が小さくて読めない。
example.english: The writing's too small to read.

examplePolite.romaji: Ji ga chiisakute yomemasen.
examplePolite.ja: 字が小さくて読めません。
examplePolite.english: The writing is too small for me to read.

notes: Kanji and kana are both ji.

use: A written character in any script, or text on a screen.

example.ja: この文字、なんて読むの？
example.english: How do you read this character?

examplePolite.romaji: Kono moji wa nan to yomu n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この文字は何と読むんですか？

notes: Overlaps with ji, but moji never means handwriting.

use: The number as written or as data, not how many there are.

example.ja: この数字、間違ってない？

examplePolite.romaji: Kono suuji, machigatte imasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: この数字、間違っていませんか？

notes: For 'how many' use kazu; suuji is the figure itself.

use: How many there are: kazu ga ooi = there are a lot.

example.romaji: Isu no kazu ga tarinai yo.
example.ja: 椅子の数が足りないよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Isu no kazu ga tarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 椅子の数が足りません。

notes: Kazoeru (to count) comes from the same root.

use: Sain suru = to sign; also a signal someone gives you.

example.ja: ここにサインしてくれる？

examplePolite.romaji: Koko ni sain o onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ここにサインをお願いします。

notes: A shop or road sign is kanban or hyoushiki, not sain.

use: After a number it includes the number: juunin ijou = ten or more people.

example.ja: 一時間以上待ったよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Ichijikan ijou machimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 一時間以上待ちました。
examplePolite.english: I waited more than an hour.

notes: Ending a talk or an order, ijou desu = 'that's all'.

example.romaji: Niku igai nara nan demo ii yo.
example.ja: 肉以外ならなんでもいいよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Niku igai nara nan demo ii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 肉以外ならなんでもいいです。

notes: Sounds the same as igai (surprising); context tells them apart.

example.ja: 十分以内に着くよ。
example.english: I'll be there within ten minutes.

examplePolite.romaji: Juppun inai ni tsukimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 十分以内に着きます。

notes: Includes the number: mikka inai = in three days or less. Sounds like inai (isn't here).

use: After an amount it means 'about': sanjuppun teido = about thirty minutes.

example.ja: ある程度はわかるよ。
example.english: I understand it to some extent.

examplePolite.romaji: Aru teido wa wakarimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ある程度はわかります。
examplePolite.english: I understand it up to a point.

notes: Aru teido = to some extent. Gurai is the casual 'about'.

english: what comes next; the rest; continuation
use: The next part of a story, show or task: tsuzuki wa ashita = the rest tomorrow.

example.ja: 続きが気になる！
example.english: I need to know what happens next!

examplePolite.romaji: Tsuzuki ga ki ni narimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 続きが気になりますね。
examplePolite.english: I really want to know what happens next.

notes: From tsuzuku (to continue). Nokori is what's left over; tsuzuki is what follows.

use: A soft, slightly childlike way to say something is finished; also ends stories.

example.ja: 今日はこれでおしまい。

examplePolite.romaji: Kyou wa kore de oshimai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はこれでおしまいです。

notes: Owari is the neutral 'end'; mou oshimai da can also mean 'it's all over for me'.

use: Mostly in compounds: saishuubi (last day), saishuukai (final episode).

example.ja: 明日が最終日だよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Ashita ga saishuubi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 明日が最終日ですよ。

notes: Saigo is the everyday 'last'; saishuu is for official endings.

english: in a row; consecutive; a series
use: Usually after a count: mikka renzoku = three days in a row.

example.romaji: Mikka renzoku de zangyou da yo.
example.ja: 三日連続で残業だよ。
example.english: That's overtime three days in a row.

examplePolite.romaji: Mikka renzoku de zangyou desu.
examplePolite.ja: 三日連続で残業です。
examplePolite.english: It's my third day in a row of overtime.

notes: Renzoku dorama = a TV drama series.

english: top; first place; the head (of a group)

example.romaji: Kanojo, kurasu de toppu nan da yo.
example.ja: 彼女、クラスでトップなんだよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Kanojo wa kurasu de toppu nan desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女はクラスでトップなんですよ。

notes: Rank or leader; the physical top of a thing is ue.

use: Usually before a noun with no: saidai no mondai = the biggest problem.

example.romaji: Sore ga saidai no mondai da yo.
example.ja: それが最大の問題だよ。

examplePolite.romaji: Sore ga saidai no mondai desu.
examplePolite.ja: それが最大の問題です。

notes: Opposite: saishou (smallest, minimum).

english: a large amount; loads; in bulk
use: Usually tairyou ni (in huge amounts) or tairyou no (a huge amount of).

example.ja: メールが大量に来てる。
example.english: I've got a ton of emails.

examplePolite.romaji: Meeru ga tairyou ni kite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: メールが大量に来ています。
examplePolite.english: A huge number of emails have come in.

notes: Everyday talk often uses ippai instead.

use: Usually before a noun with no: yuiitsu no tomodachi = my only friend.

example.romaji: Kore ga yuiitsu no shumi nan da.
example.ja: これが唯一の趣味なんだ。

examplePolite.romaji: Kore ga yuiitsu no shumi nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: これが唯一の趣味なんです。
examplePolite.english: This is my one and only hobby.

notes: Sounds a bit weighty; dake (only) is the everyday way.
